title: Reassess, Review and Repeat | Keep the Child’s Plan Accountable
software: PinnacleAI GPT-OS v1.0.0 · Class B non-diagnostic developmental-support software · licensed for children aged 0–12
parentMoment: “What changed, and what still needs a better approach?”
lifeDecision: How does today compare with the earlier observation, including setting and support, and which decision follows?
familyDiscussion: A reasoned review of progress, no change or a new need, with the next decision explained.
directAnswer: Pinnacle’s documented workflow describes periodic reassessment, updated AbilityScore and Readiness views, and plan correction. The methods preprint discusses monthly review in one programme; the right schedule for a child is a professional decision, not a universal promise.
lifePurpose: Review asks whether a skill is becoming useful in life and whether the child’s comfort, goals and context still fit the plan.

illustrativeExample.title: The child can now pack a bag—with one important exception.
illustrativeExample.description: Illustrative example only. At home the child completes most steps, while a busy school arrival still needs support.

steps.title: Compare fairly
steps.description: Look at the same ability with the support and environment clearly described.

steps.title: Listen to life
steps.description: Family and teacher observations show where the skill transfers and where it does not.

steps.title: Make a real decision
steps.description: The team may keep a useful support, change a cue, address the setting or choose a new goal.

steps.title: Check again
steps.description: Later measurement and observation test whether that decision helped.

illustrativeExample.status: Fictional explanatory example; not a patient story or observed result.

mechanism: Change, no change and decline all deserve an honest explanation.
A meaningful review connects assessed abilities to participation outside the assessment setting.
The child and family remain active partners in deciding what matters next.
limit: Repeated reassessment does not guarantee a child will become independent or receive school placement. A score change alone is not proof of a particular life outcome.

questions.question: How often should a child be reassessed?
questions.answer: A source method describes monthly reassessment in one programme. The suitable schedule depends on the child and should be agreed with the responsible professional.

questions.question: What if the score stays the same or goes down?
questions.answer: Review the measure, setting, supports, health and everyday observations. A professional and family can then decide whether to adapt the goal or support.

questions.question: Is repeating therapy until independence guaranteed?
questions.answer: No. Growing independence and participation are directions for planning. Each child’s outcomes, pace and supports differ.
